audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly named The Call of the Pack (W) as Naafiri's gap-closer and all-in engine — "Dodge The Pack (W) — it's her only gap-closer", "her W dash-in", "W-E plus packmates can one-shot you", "Dodging her W dash is the whole game". W is not a dash.
audit.why: In the kit, W carries only the untargetable flag: "Naafiri becomes Untargetable and empowers her pack, spawning additional packmates and gaining increased Move Speed and Attack Damage." The dash flags sit on E Eviscerate (450 range, 11/10/9/8/7) and on R Hounds' Pursuit (900 range, 110/95/80). Eviscerate is the gap-closer a Neeko actually has to root.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed at Eviscerate with its real range and cooldown; W now described as what it is — an untargetability plus pack empowerment on 26/24/22/20/18.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave levels 1 through 4-5 to Naafiri and the last three stages to "Skill", while content win[0..6] and packet.levelChart both read Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Naafiri/Neeko. All seven rows disagreed between layers.
audit.why: Naafiri has no all-in before her lethality item and Neeko out-ranges Darkin Daggers, so the early rows belong to Neeko; the first-item lethality spike genuinely flips one stage to her; and a single-target assassin falls off against Neeko's AoE and Zhonya's, which is the recovery the packet chart shows.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides moved onto the two agreeing sources, with every why and rating rewritten in the same proposal — including the first-item row pushed to 8/10 to mark it as the danger phase.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claimed a "3-second knockup" the kit does not give, and dosFull[2].d invited the reader to "take the fifteen-second invitation" after a spent Hounds' Pursuit.
audit.why: Hounds' Pursuit is 110/95/80 seconds. Fifteen is a fabricated number and it would get a reader killed — it tells them a spent ult is nearly back when it is not.
audit.corrected: Both removed; the real 110/95/80 now appears in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, winCon, loading and report[3].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Hounds' Pursuit recast shield was never mentioned — the exact reason a Neeko burst window fails against a committed Naafiri.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Naafiri reveals nearby enemies if she scores a takedown and can recast this Ability once. The second cast grants a shield." That shield is what absorbs the bloom you saved for her dive.
audit.corrected: Stated in enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dontsFull[2].d and content spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions says "Naafiri sustains through chip damage (Eviscerate (E)) — Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades", and report[8].t said to add anti-heal into "his sustain".
audit.why: Riot's Eviscerate text heals her PACKMATES, not Naafiri: "dashes and damages enemies in an area around her, recalling her packmates and fully healing them." Nothing in the kit says she heals herself, and whether Grievous Wounds applies to packmate healing is not answerable from this file. I did not write an anti-heal instruction on that basis.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now buys an early armour component into her first lethality spike instead of anti-heal; the pack-healing fact is left unstated rather than guessed at.

audit.whatIsWrong: Naafiri is female and the full layer called her "he/his" in tldr, winCon, ahead, breakdown.early, tradeGood, breakdown.trading, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[0].t, report[0].t, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[8].t, report[9].t, report[11].t and report[13].t.
audit.why: champ-gender lists naafiri as female, and the kit text itself says "her attacks and abilities". The content layer was already correct, so the page contradicted itself.
audit.corrected: All sixteen fields regendered as part of their rewrites.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit — catalogued defect 3 — and its one mechanical claim ("stand near minions to body-block the hounds") is not supported by anything in the kit for a lock-on ability.
audit.why: Hounds' Pursuit is described as a lock-on dash at a champion; whether minions can body-block it is not in Riot's text, so it is unknown rather than false.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the three real cooldowns; the minion-block claim dropped rather than repeated.

notes: BIGGEST FIND: the page had the wrong ability doing the gap-closing. The Call of the Pack (W) was described as her dash and all-in engine in five places across both layers; in the kit W is untargetability plus pack empowerment (26/24/22/20/18, 400 range) and the dash flags sit on Eviscerate (E, 450 range, 11/10/9/8/7) and Hounds' Pursuit (R, 900 range, 110/95/80). All five re-pointed. CHART: full-layer sides were Naafiri x4 then Skill x3 while content win[] and packet.levelChart agreed on Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Naafiri/Neeko; I brought full into line with the agreeing pair, so no content win[N] change was needed, and rewrote each why and rating alongside. FABRICATED NUMBER REMOVED: dosFull[2].d told the reader a spent Hounds' Pursuit was a "fifteen-second invitation" — it is 110s at rank 1. ANTI-HEAL NOT WRITTEN: missingInteractions asks for Grievous Wounds timing, but Riot's Eviscerate text heals her packmates, not Naafiri, and whether Grievous Wounds applies to packmate healing is not in the file — so report[8].t buys armour into her lethality spike instead. PRONOUNS: sixteen full-layer fields called her he/his. DIFF FIELD: diff="TRICKY" / 7/10 against a 50.34% win rate over 294 games looks a notch harsh, but I did not guess at the diff enum's vocabulary. LEFT ALONE: breakdown.feeding, breakdown.spikes, report[2], report[6], report[7], report[10], report[12], report[14], and content early/spikes[3]/wants.foe, all already Naafiri-specific and correctly gendered.
